Non-small-cell lung cancer accounts for about 85% of all lung cancers. As a class, non-small-cell lung cancers are relatively insensitive to chemotherapy, compared to small-cell carcinoma. [Daraxonrasib] Daraxonrasib, sold under the brand name Rasonque, is an anti-cancer medication used for the treatment of pancreatic cancer. It is an inhibitor of the RAS GTPase family. It is given by mouth. It is a small molecule RAS inhibitor of all three key members of the Ras superfamily: KRAS, HRAS, and NRAS. The three RAS proteins are GTPases that become active when bound to GTP but normally convert this GTP to GDP and thereby become inactive. RAS proteins that are bound to GDP and GTP are termed respectively RAS(OFF) and RAS(ON). It targets RAS in the ON state, but not in the OFF state. Daraxonrasib was approved for medical use in the United States in 2026. It was developed by Revolution Medicines. | other articles: 2026 in science, Pancreatic cancer
